channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Cybersecurity Officials Embarrassed by 'White-Hat' Hackers
item.description: A group calling themselves the Butterfly collective claims a supposed hack of an Uzbek government database was an exercise to expose cybersecurity flaws. They stated their goal was to improve IT defenses and that no data was stolen, despite possessing the capability. The group aims to combat malicious actors and push officials to better protect sensitive data.

item.title: US and Turkmenistan Discuss Expanding Energy Cooperation and Connectivity
item.description: US and Turkmen diplomats met in Ashgabat to discuss expanding trans-Caspian connectivity and diversifying energy exports. Turkmen officials expressed a strong desire to improve trade ties with South Asia and the West, while maintaining neutrality. Both sides reported optimistic notes on commercial ties, energy cooperation, and regional connectivity, with Turkmenistan highlighting its strategy to diversify energy supply routes.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Maintain Open Electronic Registry of Extremist Organizations and Materials
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish and maintain an open electronic registry for extremist organizations and materials. This initiative is part of broader efforts to manage the country's criminogenic situation with a new assessment model. Other news includes the revival of the '10,000 steps on foot' campaign and the main interest rate remaining unchanged at 14%.

item.title: 14-Year-Old Boy Missing in Kabul for 20 Days, Family Worried
item.description: A 14-year-old boy named Safa has been missing from the Khair Khana area of Kabul for 20 days. His family has had no contact with him since his disappearance and their efforts to find him have been unsuccessful. The boy's family is deeply worried about his whereabouts amid growing concerns over disappearances in Afghanistan.

item.title: Analysts Assess End of Trump's Political Era Following US Midterm Elections
item.description: International media are analyzing factors contributing to the Republican Party's losses in the recent US midterm elections and their potential impact on American politics. Some observers suggest this marks the end of Donald Trump's political era, while Russian military correspondents are concerned about future US-Russia relations. The election results are expected to alter America's political direction.

item.title: UNICEF and UNESCO Urge Restoration of Girls' and Women's Right to Education in Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF and UNESCO are calling for the full restoration of education rights for girls and women in Afghanistan. They warn that the continued exclusion from education, coupled with crises, is widening the gap in the education system. Without immediate action, an entire generation risks being deprived of educational opportunities, hindering future recovery and development.

item.title: Rudny Teenager Sentenced for Failing to Report a Murder
item.description: A 19-year-old from Rudny has been sentenced for concealing knowledge of a murder. The victim was stabbed to death in a residential building entrance. The court found that a teenager, who knew about the crime, fled with the suspect instead of reporting it. He was convicted of failure to report a serious crime.

item.title: UNICEF: 53% of Afghan Primary School Children Denied Education
item.description: UNICEF reports that 53% of primary school-age children in Afghanistan lack access to formal education. A joint report with UNESCO cites population growth, restrictions on girls' education, and insufficient investment as key challenges. Afghanistan remains the only country barring girls from education beyond primary level.

item.title: World Firefighting and Rescue Sports Championship Draw Held in Baku
item.description: The draw for the XXI World Championship for men and XII for women in firefighting and rescue sports took place in Baku. Over 400 athletes from more than 20 countries, including Uzbekistan, are participating. Uzbekistan's team, a past world champion, is among the leaders in the sport.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Index of Criminal Situation Using Facial Recognition Technology
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce an index of the criminal situation based on facial recognition technology. President Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to improve crime prevention, noting the installation of 263,000 cameras and 70,000 intercoms. A new draft law on crime prevention is also being prepared.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reviews Public Security Mechanisms and Considers New Law
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its public security system with modern requirements, including 263,000 surveillance cameras and 70,000 intercoms. Efforts have improved conditions in 701 out of 809 high-crime neighborhoods. The government is considering a new draft law on crime prevention to address evolving threats like cybercrime, as the current 2014 law requires updates.

item.title: Uzbekistan Showcases Tourism Potential at World Travel Market in London
item.description: Uzbekistan is promoting its diverse tourism offerings, from cultural heritage to gastronomic and adventure travel, at the World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026. The national stand features 11 participants, including Uzbekistan Airways and nine tourism companies. Emphasis is placed on promoting traditional routes and new experiences.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tax Committee Explains Bank Account Freezes After Mobile Transfers Scrutiny
item.description: Kazakhstan's State Revenue Committee has clarified why some citizens' bank accounts are being blocked after mobile transfer checks. Account freezes occur when taxpayers fail to respond to notifications within 30 working days. The committee conducts regular checks on POS terminal and mobile transfer data against tax declarations.

item.title: Pakistan Envoy Discusses Afghanistan's Humanitarian Crisis with UN Refugee Agency
item.description: Pakistan's Special Representative for Afghanistan, Muhammad Sadiq, met with the new UNHCR representative in Pakistan, Noriko Takagi. They discussed Afghanistan's humanitarian situation, major challenges, and the importance of international cooperation amid the country's crises and difficult economic conditions.

item.title: AI Model of World Ocean to Be Created for Climate Change Studies
item.description: A Chilean center of the French Institute of Digital Science and Technology has received $2.5 million from an American company to build an AI model of the world's oceans. The model will help predict climate change impacts more accurately by learning from physical, biological, and genomic data. It aims to forecast changes in marine life and provide early warnings for harmful algal blooms and coral bleaching.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards Tajik Parliament Speaker Rustami Emomali with Order
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Rustami Emomali, Chairman of the National Assembly of Tajikistan, who arrived on an official visit. They discussed deepening bilateral relations and parliamentary cooperation. Mirziyoyev awarded Emomali the "Fidokorona xizmatlari uchun" order for his contributions to strengthening strategic partnership and parliamentary dialogue.

item.title: Uzbek President Congratulates Farmers on Exceeding 5 Million Tons of Cotton Harvest
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated farmers for producing over 5 million tons of cotton. Cotton yield in Uzbekistan has increased 2.7 times, reaching 56 centners per hectare. Farmers are expected to achieve a net profit of 13-14 trillion Uzbek soums from cotton this year.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ready to Export Up to 500,000 Tons of Wheat to Israel
item.description: Kazakhstan is prepared to consider supplying between 200,000 and 500,000 tons of food wheat and other agricultural products to Israel. This was discussed at the tenth meeting of the Kazakhstan-Israel Intergovernmental Commission in Jerusalem. "Prodcorporation" is ready to discuss long-term contracts based on Israeli market demand.

item.title: Toll Road Fees in Kazakhstan May Increase by Up to 50%
item.description: Toll road fees in Kazakhstan are planned to be gradually increased between 2027 and 2029, with the Ministry of Transport intending to review tariffs annually. Fees for vehicles in classes 2-5 could rise by up to 30%, while those for heavy trucks (class 6-7) might increase by up to 50%.

item.title: Iran Issues Nuclear Attack Preparedness Guide for Public
item.description: Iran has distributed guidelines for the public in case of a nuclear explosion, including an eight-minute instructional video. Prepared by Isfahan province emergency services, the guide advises on protection from blast waves, finding shelter, and avoiding radioactive contamination. Residents are urged to stay in shelters for at least 24 hours and use bottled water and sealed food.

item.title: Moscow Format for Afghan Issues Discussed Amid Regional Tensions
item.description: The Moscow Format, a platform for discussing Afghan issues, was a topic of discussion. This comes amid broader regional dynamics, including US sanctions impacting Iran's trade with Afghanistan and neighboring countries. Separately, UNHCR reported that 6.3 million Afghans have returned since 2023, with 60 percent reportedly forced.

item.title: French Blood Service Refrigerators Hacked, Plasma Exposed to High Temperatures
item.description: Hackers breached the systems of a French Blood Service contractor, altering refrigerator settings to +110 degrees Celsius instead of the required -30 degrees for plasma. An alarm alerted staff, preventing critical temperature rises. Some plasma was moved to other storage facilities as investigations begin.

item.title: Former Minister Bishimbayev's Mother Sues Ex-Wife for 22 Million Tenge
item.description: The mother of convicted former minister Kuanysh Bishimbayev has filed a fifth lawsuit against his ex-wife, Nazym Kaharman, demanding 22 million tenge. The dispute concerns commercial property managed by Kaharman during their marriage. She claims funds earned were used for children's needs and were previously agreed upon.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards Tajik Parliament Speaker for Strengthening Ties
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has awarded Rustam Emomali, the Chairman of the Tajik Parliament's upper house, the "Fidokorona xizmatlari uchun" order. The award recognizes Emomali's contributions to strengthening strategic partnership and alliance between Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Inspects Dilapidated Kindergarten and School in Qarshi
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, visited Qarshi in the Qashqadaryo region. She inspected a kindergarten in a dilapidated state and a cold school, vowing to address these issues promptly. Plans include building a new kindergarten and renovating the school.

item.title: Teenager Sentenced to Prison for Failing to Report Murder in Rudny
item.description: A court in Kazakhstan's Kostanay region sentenced two residents of Rudny, including a minor, for a murder case. The murder occurred on January 23rd, with one defendant stabbing the victim over 200,000 tenge. The minor, who was on a lower floor, did not report the crime. The convicted murderer received nine years, and the minor received two years and eight months.

item.title: Police Detain Protesters in Astana Demanding Action on Election Results
item.description: In Astana, approximately twenty individuals who gathered to voice grievances were detained by police. The protest appears to be related to the recent US midterm elections and their potential impact on President Trump's foreign policy. The exact reasons for the detentions were not immediately clear.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Inspects Facilities in Qashqadaryo Region, Uzbekistan
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva visited schools, kindergartens, a canal, and a narcology center in the Qashqadaryo region. Plans include building a new 360-capacity kindergarten in Qarshi and renovating School No. 43. The 'Chap Tarmok' canal will be concreted, and a program to reform the region's narcology services is being developed.

item.title: UN Deputy Special Representative Rabab Fatima Visits Eastern Afghanistan to Assess Needs
item.description: UNAMA Deputy Special Representative Rabab Fatima visited eastern Afghanistan, including border areas, from October 27-29 to understand local needs and challenges. She met with residents, including women, to discuss their concerns and opportunities for improvement. Fatima reiterated the UN's commitment to supporting the Afghan people.

item.title: Kazakh IT Company's AI Projects Highly Valued at UAE Energy Exhibition
item.description: Kazakhstan's TrustExam.ai presented its artificial intelligence platform for remote testing of oil and gas company employees at the ADIPEC 2026 exhibition in Abu Dhabi. The solution helps enterprises systematically verify knowledge in health, safety, and environmental protection (HSE), adapting to various production facilities and shift teams.

item.title: Group of Serial Cattle Rustlers Detained in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar Region
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region have detained a group of individuals suspected of serial cattle rustling. Over several months, the suspects allegedly committed more than five episodes of theft, stealing horses and cattle. During searches, stolen livestock and vehicles were recovered.

item.title: Uzbekistan Emergency Academy Hosts 'Meeting of Three Generations' for Cadets
item.description: The Academy of the Ministry of Emergency Situations in Uzbekistan organized a 'Meeting of Three Generations' to pass on experience from veterans to young servicemen. The academy chief emphasized the importance of generational continuity and fostering loyalty to the homeland. Recommendations were given on decisive action in complex situations.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Coxsackie Virus Not Registered as Separate Disease, Health Committee States
item.description: Uzbekistan's Sanitary-Epidemiological Committee, through representative Nurmat Otabekov, announced that the Coxsackie virus is not officially registered as a distinct illness. While often mild, the virus can cause complications like pneumonia and meningitis in some patients, according to the committee.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belarus Agree to Strengthen Strategic Partnership and Discuss Eurasian Security
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belarus reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing political dialogue and bilateral cooperation. The countries signed a cooperation plan between their foreign ministries for 2027-2028. Discussions also covered Eurasian security, with Kazakhstan emphasizing mutual trust and international law.

item.title: US Midterm Elections Shape Central Asia's Economic and Diplomatic Agenda
item.description: Democrats' control of Congress following the US midterms inherits a Central Asia agenda focused on economic ties. Substantial orders for American manufacturers from Uzbekistan Airways and Kazakhstan's Wabtec agreement highlight the region's importance for US exports and jobs, influencing diplomatic engagement.

item.title: Shymkent discusses tasks set in the Head of State's Address
item.description: An asset meeting in Shymkent, chaired by city akim Gabit Syzdykbekov, discussed President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's Address "Current Tasks of Kazakhstan at a New Historical Stage." The address outlines strategic development goals, requiring focused work on the ground to strengthen the economy, modernize infrastructure, and improve living standards.

item.title: Shymkent Discusses Tasks Outlined in President's Address to the Nation
item.description: An active meeting in Shymkent, chaired by Mayor Gabit Syzdykbekov, discussed President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." Participants, including officials and public figures, focused on strengthening the economy, modernizing infrastructure, and improving living standards.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Georgia Enhance Trade and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Tashkent's Deputy Khokim met with the Georgian Ambassador to discuss boosting trade, investment, and industrial cooperation. Emphasis was placed on increasing mutual trade volumes, launching new investment projects, and fostering direct contacts between entrepreneurs. Opportunities for Georgian companies in Tashkent's industrial zones and urban development were also explored.

item.title: Uzbek Students Participate in Space Experiments in Moscow
item.description: A team from Uzbekistan's Tashkent Institute of Irrigation and Agricultural Mechanization Engineers successfully presented a scientific-engineering project at the "ORBITA-2026" international space games in Moscow. The project involved studying the adaptation of living organisms to extreme conditions and performing tasks related to autonomous life support and engineering in simulated Martian missions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Agriculture Ministry Seeks Resumption of Enterprise Certification by Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture is seeking the resumption of certification for its enterprises by Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor. A meeting between veterinary service officials discussed further steps to ensure Kyrgyz products access to the Russian market, veterinary control, and the supply of veterinary medicines and biological preparations.
